failure_modes: Turkey problem: a model fits every available data point and is catastrophically wrong, because the relevant information lies outside the agent's position in information space
Confusing complicated with complex, and treating a hard but closed problem as open
Spending effort to close the gap instead of detecting when the {{model_as_compression}} has expired
gloss: Complexity is the gap between a bounded model and an open world, and it does not close
invariants: Complexity is a relation between a model and its world, not a property of the world alone
The gap cannot be closed, only managed
Every model has a valid-until date, whether or not it is known
mechanism: Every {{model_as_compression}} is bounded by resources and by what it incorporated when it was built. The world it models is open: exogenous effects arise from what the model never included, and a model cannot fully account for itself. Complexity names this gap. {{computational_irreducibility}}, observer effects and reflexivity hold it open. Every model therefore carries a valid-until date, and the practical question is how a system detects that its model has expired.
